IRAN WAR DIARY, Day 35

5 weeks. No ceasefire. No off-ramp. Just escalation.

Here's where we stand on April 4, 2026:

MILITARY

Iran shot down a US F-15E Strike Eagle over central Iran. First American aircraft lost over Iranian territory in this war. One crew member rescued, one WSO still missing. An A-10 Warthog also went down near the Strait, pilot rescued. Two Black Hawks took small arms fire during the rescue.

US and Israel hit the Pasteur Institute (a century-old medical research center in Tehran), the B1 bridge in Karaj (13 killed, 100+ injured), and steel plants across the country. Iran says a Red Crescent aid warehouse in Bushehr was also struck by drone.

Iran fired its largest missile barrage in weeks at Israel. 14 wounded near Tel Aviv including an 11 year old girl. Fire at industrial site in southern Negev. Ben Gurion Airport at reduced capacity. Schools moved online nationwide.

Iran's total casualties since Feb 28: 2,076 killed, 26,500 wounded. Over 600 schools and education centers hit.

DIPLOMACY (OR LACK OF IT)

Iran rejected a US proposal for a 48 hour ceasefire. Their response wasn't written. It was delivered through continued attacks. Trust between both sides sits at "zero" according to Iran's FM Araghchi.

Ceasefire talks have reached a dead end. Iran told mediators it won't meet US officials in Islamabad. Iran's demands: reparations, US withdrawal from Middle East bases, guarantees against future attacks. Trump's position: "We will consider when the Hormuz Strait is open, free, and clear."

Meanwhile, Hegseth fired the Army's top general, Randy George, plus two other senior officers. Mid war. Senator Murphy: "Experienced generals are telling Hegseth his Iran war plans are unworkable."

HORMUZ

2,000+ ships stranded. 27 commercial vessels attacked since March 1. 11 seafarers dead. But cracks appearing: a French CMA CGM container ship crossed the Strait (first Western vessel since the war). Three Omani tankers and the first Japanese LNG carrier also made it through.

Iran is playing favorites: China, Russia, India, Pakistan, Malaysia, Thailand, Philippines all granted passage. The US and Israel? Still locked out.

UN Security Council vote on Bahrain's proposal to reopen the Strait happening today. Russia and China hold veto power and remain uncommitted.

ECONOMICS

Brent crude at $112/barrel. The war has cost Arab countries $120 194 billion in GDP in one month (UNDP). Israel's wars since Oct 2023 have cost $112 billion. Australia is running out of diesel. Global food prices up 2.4% in March.

Trump just requested a $1.5 trillion defense budget for 2027.

$BTC hovering at ~$67K. Still 47% down from its ATH. Every risk asset is hostage to Hormuz.

The most dangerous part of this war isn't the missiles.

It's that nobody has a plan to end it.

#IranWarDiary

Rice, Nutrition, and Preventive Health Education in the Philippines
- Dr. Tony Leachon 

The Philippines is not poor. We have fertile lands, abundant rice, and resilient farmers. What we lack is judicious stewardship of resources. Funds must never be stolen; they must be used wisely for the poor, the needy, and the vulnerable. Rice should not be wasted—it should be rechanneled to malnourished children and stunted youth, who represent the nation’s future.

Preventing Wastage and Redirecting Resources

• Half rice servings in restaurants: Normalize smaller portions to reduce waste and prevent overeating.
• Discourage “eat-all-you-can” buffets: Shift cultural norms toward moderation and mindful eating.
• Community feeding programs: Redirect surplus rice to schools and barangays, pairing it with vegetables and protein for balanced nutrition.

Tackling Malnutrition and Obesity

The country faces a double burden: malnutrition and stunting among children, and obesity-driven diseases among adults. Solutions must be holistic:

• Nutrition education: Teach portion control, balanced diets, and dangers of overconsumption.
• Calorie counters and front-of-pack labels (UK model): Clear, color-coded nutrition labels to guide healthier choices.
• Walkable environments: Build pedestrian-friendly cities to encourage daily physical activity.

Embedding Preventive Health Education in DEPED and CHED

Preventive health must be part of the curriculum:

• Smoking, vaping, and alcohol awareness: Highlight long-term risks and promote abstinence or moderation.
• Good nutrition and calorie literacy: Equip students with tools to monitor intake and make healthier choices.
• Practical life skills: Encourage active lifestyles and responsible consumption habits.

Global Best Practices

• UK traffic-light nutrition labels: Simple, effective guidance on fat, sugar, and salt.
• Japan’s school lunch program: Balanced meals nationwide, teaching lifelong healthy eating habits.
• Brazil’s dietary guidelines: Emphasize fresh, minimally processed foods, discourage ultra-processed products.
• Singapore’s Healthier Choice Symbol: Government-backed labeling to nudge consumers toward healthier packaged foods.

Conclusion

Rice is more than food—it is a symbol of sustenance and abundance. By preventing waste, redirecting resources to malnourished children, and embedding preventive health education into schools, the Philippines can fight hunger and obesity simultaneously. 

With global best practices adapted to local realities, we can build a healthier, more resilient nation where food security and public health go hand in hand.
